topics.topic: How flow endpoint directions are handled between prove_version phases 3 and 5
questions: Must phase 5 explicitly treat a flow input as a permitted source and a flow output as a permitted target, or must phase 3 instead require output-to-input directions for flow endpoints?
Must phase 5 treat flow inputs as dataflow outputs and flow outputs as dataflow inputs despite their stored PortDirection, or must its wording be changed to state the endpoint exception explicitly?

quotes: - prove_version: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run nine phases in this fixed order and return at the first failing check, items within a phase in that phase's order and conditions of one item in the order listed: 1 nodes by node_id, a function node names a contract version that read_contract_version finds and an operation node names a binding that read_binding finds with status accepted; 2 constants by to_node then to_port, the port exists and is an input port of a node, never a flow output, of value carriage, the constant's declared value_schema equals the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema text for a one port, the canonical array schema with it as items for a many port) — composition already refused a value that does not fit its declared schema, so no separate value check runs here; 3 edges in edge order, the source exists as an output port of a node or an input port of the flow, then the target as an input port of a node or an output port of the flow, a port of the other direction not counting, and both carry equal value_schema text, the same carriage and for files the same media type, a flow endpoint port being value carriage; 4 guards in edge order, the guard port is an output of one cardinality of the edge's source node, that node has no map_over, its schema is a closed set with enum or const, and the guard value is a member: guard_value is canonical JSON text, and it is a member when its UTF-8 bytes equal canonical_bytes of the JSON text of one enum member or of the const (bytes compared with bytes).

- prove_version: [BEHAVIOR] Phase 5 cardinality in edge order: a one output feeds a one input, a many output feeds a many input or the one input that is its node's map_over port, a one output never feeds a many input, every output of a node with map_over counts as many for its consumers, and a node with map_over has exactly that input fed that way and no output of many cardinality; phase 6 fan-in by to_node then to_port: every input port of every node and every flow output has at least one edge or constant, a port with a constant has no other constant and no edge, and no two edges that can both deliver end at one port, two edges being unable to both deliver only when both are guarded on the same guard port of the same source node with different guard values.
judgement.divergence: One implementer treats flow inputs as phase-5 dataflow outputs and flow outputs as phase-5 dataflow inputs, applying cardinality checks to endpoint edges; another interprets phase 5 by stored PortDirection and rejects or omits those endpoint edges from its output-to-input rules. The owner or caller notices different ProofResult outcomes for the same flow version.
judgement.why: Phase 3 expressly gives flow endpoints direction exceptions, while phase 5 uses output/input terminology without saying whether those exceptions continue to apply.
